content.comment_body: Hello, I'm back with a new issue. I've added another [product_name] unit to my setup, which currently includes three inverters communicating over modbus to the [product_name] and then the [product_name] controller. I added the second [product_name] in order to set up additional communication channels, allowing me to monitor voltage, current, and speed for all three inverters. However, when trying to read voltage, current, and speed values from inverters 2 and 3 using the second [product_name], I'm only seeing incorrect readings. It's worth noting that I can start, stop, and set/read frequency on inverters 2 and 3 using channels configured in the first [product_name] without any problems, so I'm almost certain the issue is with the second [product_name], but I can't pinpoint what went wrong. Both [product_name] units have unique IP addresses and can establish a connection to the [product_name] controller. I'm accessing the correct areas on inverters 2 and 3, so could my wiring be at fault? I joined the modbus A&B pins from the first [product_name] directly to the A&B pins on the second one. Any advice would be much appreciated. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is having trouble integrating two [product_name] modules with a single [product_name] controller for monitoring three inverters via Modbus. While the first [product_name] communicates flawlessly, the second one returns inaccurate readings from the inverters. The user suspects a wiring issue but hasn't found the cause yet, and there is no clear solution or suggestion available in the discussion so far.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to connect multiple [product_name] modules to a single [product_name] controller and retrieve accurate inverter data through Modbus. They are looking for confirmation regarding proper wiring and configuration, as well as a reliable way to receive correct readings from all connected devices.
